description: A rounded shrub 1.5-3 m tall with large, smooth, bright green leaves in pairs that smell of spice when crushed, and through spring and summer dark maroon-red flowers like small water lilies at the branch tips, followed by brown, urn-shaped seed pods. It grows along the shaded creeks and seeps of the foothills and canyons, where its flowers smell of old wine.

season_notes.winter: Bare smooth grey-brown stems with last year's woody brown urn-shaped pods still on them.
season_notes.spring: Big bright leaves in March and April; the first maroon flowers open in April.
season_notes.summer: Flowers on and off into August, scented like wine; beetles crawl in and out of them.
season_notes.fall: Leaves turn yellow and drop; the pods harden and hang on.

riparian.water: Wants moist soil all year in part shade: the banks of small permanent creeks, springs and seeps in canyon bottoms.

notes: Western spicebush is a California endemic, a deciduous shrub 1-4 m of streambanks, seeps and moist canyon bottoms in the North Coast Ranges, the Sierra Nevada foothills and the Cascades, usually in part shade with alder, maple and dogwood. Form: plain 'shrub'. Five to nine smooth, upright stems from the base that spread by root sprouts (stems [5, 9], stem_spread 32), branching in opposite pairs (rotation -90) into a rounded clump about as wide as tall. Bark smooth, grey-brown (bark_pattern smooth_grey); the stems and leaves are aromatic, a camphor-and-spice smell. Leaves opposite, ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 5-15 cm, entire, rough to the touch above but somewhat shiny, bright green, yellow in fall: leaf_shape oval, leaf_size_m 0.12. Flowers solitary at the branch tips, 4-7 cm, with many strap-shaped tepals, dark red to maroon fading brownish, scented of wine, pollinated by small beetles, April-August: flowers form cluster (a single blossom at a time), size_m 0.05, density 0.25 (only a few open at once). Fruit an urn- or bell-shaped woody receptacle 2-4 cm holding the seeds, brown, staying on into winter: berries form bud, brown, months [9, 2]. The plant contains calycanthine, which is toxic, and is little browsed: no eaten_by. Zones: bank, then terrace; small permanent creeks and springs, orders [2, 4], perennial. shades_water 0.2.
